claims.title: The Laguna Copperplate Inscription
claims.summary: Dated to 900 CE, the earliest known Philippine document records a debt remission and reveals an organised society of datus and nobles already linked to the wider Malay and Javanese world.

sources.label: Philippines (country overview and history)

claims.title: Founding of the Sultanate of Sulu
claims.summary: Islam takes political form as the Sultanate of Sulu rises around Jolo, becoming a powerful maritime state controlling trade across the Sulu Sea and toward Borneo.

claims.title: Islam consolidates in Maguindanao
claims.summary: The conversion of ruling families on Mindanao, associated with the missionary Sharif Muhammad Kabungsuwan, founds the Sultanate of Maguindanao, which expands through the 16th and 17th centuries.

claims.title: Legazpi founds the first Spanish settlement at Cebu
claims.summary: Miguel Lopez de Legazpi establishes Spain's first permanent settlement in the islands at Cebu, beginning more than three centuries of Spanish colonial rule.

claims.title: Founding of Manila
claims.summary: Legazpi establishes Manila as the capital of the Spanish colony; by the century's end most lowland Luzon and the Visayas are under Spanish control.

claims.title: The Manila-Acapulco galleon trade
claims.summary: For 250 years Spanish galleons exchange Chinese silks for Mexican silver across the Pacific, making Manila a hub of global commerce and an economic lifeline for the colony.

claims.summary: By the Treaty of Paris ending the Spanish-American War, Spain cedes the Philippines to the United States without consulting Filipinos, who had already declared independence.
